notes: A.1 item 146 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD clause (calculations to derive size of records on storage medium)' -> OK §A.1 146): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR2 'The implementor shall specify the calculations necessary for the user to derive the size for records on the storage medium' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 2)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-146 row (audit_annex_a1.py does not list 146). The only related text is DOC-A.1-151 (4-byte LE length prefix for variable-length record sequential/relative/indexed; line delimiters for LINE SEQUENTIAL), which answers GR5 of §12.4.5.11 for VARIABLE records only and states no calculation for fixed-length files, nor for CODE-SET's effect (GR2 names CODE-SET and FORMAT as factors). Probe probe/rec/p1.cob: fixed FD F1 (01 X(5)) writes two unframed 5-byte records (10-byte file); implicit Format 1 F4 (X(5)+X(10)) pads every record to 10 bytes unframed; Format 3 F3 writes 4-byte-prefixed frames (0x05000000 'ABCDE' ...). So the calculation is fixed in code (fixed: record size; variable: 4 + record size) but not documented. Harm silent. Owning note kb/Work PB1278 (open, claims item 146) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 147 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD clause (implicit RECORD clause if RECORD clause is not specified)' -> OK §A.1 147): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR5 'This implicit RECORD clause is defined by the implementor' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 5)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-147 row. A determination exists only in prose outside the register: §3 D-FRA (iv) ('the implicit RECORD clause ... is Format 2 when a record is variable-length ... and Format 1 otherwise'), which audit_annex_a1.py does not count and no inventory anchor resolves to. Code: FileModel.ImpliesVariableFormat = Varying is null && RecordContains is null && any variable-length record; else implied Format 1 at the largest record. Probe probe/rec/p1.cob F4 (01 X(5), 01 X(10), no RECORD clause): both records written as 10 bytes, consistent with GR5 a). Edges NOT conforming per kb/Work PB1276 (row GR-13.18.43.4-5 PARTIAL: implied Format 2 minimum inherits the GR8 national byte-count defect) and PB322 determination F (a RECORD-clause-less SD releases at record-name-1's own size) — cited, not re-reported. Harm silent (the missing §7 row). No kb/Work note claims DOC-A.1-147 (PB1278 claims 146/148 only; PB1276 mentions item 147 but its inventory_rows do not include it) — NEW finding, clustered with PB1278.

A.1 item 148 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 148): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR17 'It is implementor defined whether format 3 of the RECORD clause produces fixed-length records or variable-length records' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 17)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-148 row, and no prose elsewhere states the choice. Code answers VARIABLE: probe probe/rec/p1.cob FD F3 RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 10 CHARACTERS writes a 5-byte and a 10-byte record as two 4-byte-length-prefixed frames (0x05 00 00 00 'ABCDE' 0x0A 00 00 00 'ABCDEFGHIJ'), i.e. variable-length. Behaviour is fixed but undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Same framing re-probed at --std 85 (identical bytes). Owning note kb/Work PB1278 (open, claims item 148) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 149 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD DELIMITER clause (consistency rules when used with external file connectors)' -> OK §A.1 149): CONDITIONALLY required, 'conditioned upon the existence of the optional feature-name in the RECORD DELIMITER clause'. The rule it points at is §12.4.5.3 GR1 c) (A.1 writes '12.4.5, General rule 1c'): 'The implementor shall specify the consistency rules for feature-name-1' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 -> OK 1) c)). A.1 preamble: 'Conditionally required: If the associated feature or language element is implemented then this element is also required.' (verbatim in §A.1 preamble). The feature is NOT implemented: docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-150 records feature-name-1 as 'Not provided.' (empty set; a written feature-name is accepted-inert with COBOLNET1778, §2 row 26 declines the whole RECORD DELIMITER clause). So the obligation cannot be incurred — but §7 has NO DOC-A.1-149 row saying so, and no derived-verdicts selector covers a CONDITIONALLY-required item whose condition is absent (a1-optional-not-provided selects requirement=optional only; evaluated with scripts/spec/inventory_schema.DerivedSelector over this row: not selected). Whether such a row closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT (by a §7 'Not provided — condition absent' row, or by extending PB280 Q1's selector to the conditionally-required class) is an owner decision, not an adjudicator's. Owning register: kb/Work A11 (open). No per-item note found (grep 'item 149' / 'DOC-A.1-149' over kb/Work: none).

A.1 item 152 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 152): CONDITIONALLY required, 'conditioned on the existence of such circumstances in an implementation'; documented if provided. §9.1.16: 'The implementor may specify circumstances other than a locked logical record that result in the return of a locked record status.' (cite.py --check 9.1.16 -> OK). Code read: status 51 (FileStatusCode.RecordLocked) is produced at exactly two sites — PhysicalFileTable.LockRecord (the record id is held by ANOTHER connector) and FileRegistry.ConflictOnLockedRecord (IsLockedByOther on the target record id); the FileRegistry.cs:1635 use only compares it for RETRY FOREVER. Locks are per logical record id (no block / index-reorganization locking), so no other circumstance returns 51: the implementation provides NO such circumstances and the condition is absent. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has no DOC-A.1-152 row stating that, and no derived-verdicts selector covers a CONDITIONALLY-required A.1 item whose condition is absent (a1-optional-not-provided is requirement=optional only; DerivedSelector evaluated over this row: not selected). Whether this closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT / CONFORMS on a 'None.' §7 row, or via a class selector, is an owner decision (same question as DOC-A.1-149). Editions: record locking exists from 2002 (Annex E), not probed per edition. Owning register kb/Work A11; no per-item note (grep 'item 152'/'DOC-A.1-152' over kb/Work: none).

A.1 item 154 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 154): required, at least 255, documented. §12.4.5.9.4 GR7 (A.1 writes '12.4.5.9, LOCK MODE clause, General rule 7'): 'The implementor shall specify the maximum number of record locks that may be held by a run unit; that maximum shall be at least 255' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 -> OK 7)). Code: PhysicalFileTable.RunUnitLockMax = 255; LockRecord and PreflightNewLock return 53 (RunUnitLockLimit) when TotalRunUnitLocks() >= 255 (the table is one instance per FileRegistry, i.e. per run unit). The value meets the >= 255 floor and the 'unsuccessful ... I-O status that indicates that condition' half returns 53. Pinned by unit:CobolFileLockTests.RunUnitLockLimit_256thRunUnitLock_Is53. BUT docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-154 row, and grep of CONFORMANCE.md for '255'/'53'/lock ceiling finds no statement of the run-unit maximum anywhere => the required documentation is absent: DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 154 (PB707 is about the RETRY path of 53/54, inventory_rows []; PB671 is citation labels) — NEW finding.

A.1 item 155 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 155): required, at least 15, documented. §12.4.5.9.4 GR7: 'The implementor shall specify the maximum number of record locks that may be held by a file connector; that maximum shall be at least 15' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 -> OK 7)). Code: PhysicalFileTable.ConnectorLockMax = 15; LockRecord / PreflightNewLock count the locks the connector name holds on the physical file and return 54 (ConnectorLockLimit) at the 16th. Meets the >= 15 floor; pinned by unit:CobolFileLockTests.ConnectorLockLimit_16thRecord_Is54. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-155 row and no statement of the per-connector maximum anywhere => DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 155 — NEW finding (same mechanism as DOC-A.1-154).

A.1 item 156 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 156): required + documented (A.1 cites 'Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b'). §6.1: 'The implementor shall specify any control characters that terminate a free-form line' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 b)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-156 row (the only reference-format row is DOC-A.1-158, margin R) and no prose elsewhere names the free-form line terminators. Code: NormalizeToFreeFormMapped splits the source on '\n' and each free-form segment line is TrimEnd('\r') (ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs:108/172), so LF terminates a line and a CR immediately before it is dropped; no other control character (FF, VT, lone CR) is a terminator. A fixed answer exists but is undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Editions: free-form reference format exists from 2002 (Annex E). Owning note kb/Work PB1496 (open; its title names item 156 and its fixer owes the DOC-A.1-156 row) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 157 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 157): required + documented (A.1 cites 'Clause 6, Reference format, rule 1c'). §6.1: 'The implementor shall specify the meaning of lines and character positions' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 c)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-157 row; DOC-A.1-158 fixes only margin R (col 72) and does not say what a line or a character position IS (record vs LF-delimited line, one UTF-16 code unit vs byte per position, whether a short fixed-form record is padded to margin R). Code: a line is an LF-delimited segment of the decoded source text (CR trimmed); a character position is one char of that string; a fixed-form line's program-text area is line[7..] truncated to 65 but NEVER padded to margin R — which kb/Work PB1491 measures as a wrong answer for a continued literal (GnuCOBOL/IBM pad) — and a free-form line over the §6.1 a) 255-position maximum is accepted silently (kb/Work PB1496). Undocumented, with an edge in dispute => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning notes kb/Work PB1496 (open; its fixer owes the DOC-A.1-157 row) and PB1491 (open; the padding behaviour the row must state) — cited, not re-reported.

ABCD
' — each print line is CRLF-delimited text through the sequential connector's advancing writer (SequentialConnector NewLine="
"), no length prefix, whatever ORGANIZATION. The structure is fixed but undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note kb/Work PB1253 (open; title names item 159, fixer owes the DOC-A.1-159 row) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 160 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 160): required + documented. §13.18.14.4 GR2: 'There is a fixed correspondence, specified by the implementor, between a column and a character in a national character set.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK 2)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-160 row and no other statement of the column/national-character correspondence. Fixed but undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Editions: national (PIC N) exists from 2002. Owning note kb/Work PB1253 (open; title names item 160) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 161 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 161): required + documented. §12.3.8.4 GR6: 'It is implementor-defined how the information in the class specifier and the external repository are used to determine which class is used.' (cite.py --check 12.3.8.4 -> OK 6)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-161 row (the neighbouring DOC-A.1-163 row covers only when AS is required). Code: there is no §8.13 external repository; a REPOSITORY class-specifier is recorded by DataBinder.BindDeclarations and never resolved there, and OoNameResolution.Resolve looks the name up only in the compilation group's own OoClassTable at a USE (COBOLNET0813/0821 when absent) — so a class compiled elsewhere is never found through the repository. The item cannot be settled by documentation alone: kb/Work PB1086 (open, blocked_by PB1099; inventory_rows include GR-12.3.8.4-6) is BLOCKED on owner question PB1099 Q3 (status: owner) — 'implement §8.13's external repository, or document a determination for Annex A.1 items 66/161/162?'. Until the owner answers, the determination this row needs does not exist. Cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 167 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 167): conditionally required, 'conditioned upon support for non-COBOL modules', and 'shall be documented'. §14.6.1: 'A run unit may additionally contain runtime modules and data storage areas derived from the compilation of compilation units written in languages other than COBOL; in this case the requirements for the relationship and interaction between the COBOL and the non-COBOL modules are defined by the implementor.' (cite.py --check 14.6.1 -> OK). The CONDITION IS MET: docs/CONFORMANCE.md itself names a supported non-COBOL component — a .NET host that invokes a generated program class directly instead of entering through ProgramTable.RunMain (§3 bullet on §14.9.18.4 GR1 a), ~line 450) — and DOC-A.1-19 (CANCEL of a non-COBOL program: no effect) / DOC-A.1-134 (MODULE-NAME of a non-COBOL module) answer neighbouring single questions. But there is NO DOC-A.1-167 row stating the run-unit relationship itself: whether a .NET host shares one RunUnit (RunUnit.Current / ResetCurrent) across activations, how its storage and switches/locale relate to the run unit, what a host must do to start/end a run unit, and whether a CALL can reach a non-COBOL module (the §3 bullet says it cannot — no CALL-CONVENTION). Scattered partial answers, no determination under this item => DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 167 (PB1149 owns §14.2.3 GR13 non-COBOL activator restrictions + §14.9.23.4 GR2 b); PB1253 owns item 116; PB1069 owns run-unit state scoping) — NEW finding, clustered with PB1149.

A.1 item 168 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 168): required + documented. §14.6.11 GR5: 'If a locale was in use in the run unit, the implementor specifies whether the locale is reset to the locale in effect when the run unit was activated.' (cite.py --check 14.6.11 -> OK 5)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-168 row and no other statement. Code: the run unit's locale lives in RunUnit.Locale (a LocaleState instance member); SET LOCALE / LocaleManager.SetLocale write it and never touch the process CultureInfo; RunUnit.ResetCurrent resets only Programs and Random, so on the emitted driver path a SET LOCALE done by run unit 1 SURVIVES into the next run unit a host starts in the same process — the answer is effectively 'not reset', and it is not a chosen one (kb/Work PB1069 measures it as a wrong answer). Undocumented + behaviour not settled => DIVERGES, harm silent. Editions: SET LOCALE / locale facility from 2002. Owning note kb/Work PB1069 (open; its body says item 168's determination 'follows from this note's LOCALE-state scoping fix and is owed with it') — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 169 (cite.py --check A.1 'SAME SORT/SORT-MERGE AREA clause (extent of allocation)' -> OK §A.1 169): 'This item is required. The internal procedure employed by the implementor does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' — so (a) no §7 determination is owed, and none exists. §12.4.6.4.4 GR4 b): 'Storage areas assigned to files specified in a sort-merge-area format SAME clause that do not represent sort or merge files may be allocated as needed for sorting or merging ... The extent of such allocation shall be specified by the implementor.' (cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 -> OK 4) b)). (b) Behaviour: the implementation's extent is NONE — DataBinder.BindIoControl binds only Format 2 (SAME RECORD AREA) and passes over the sort-merge-area format (`same.RECORD() is null` -> continue), so no non-sort file's storage is ever taken for sorting; SORT/MERGE work storage is the runtime's own managed memory. 'may be allocated' makes zero a permitted extent; GR4 c) (non-sort files do not share storage with each other) holds trivially since the format creates no sharing, and GR4 a) reuse among the named sort files is internal and unobservable. Probe probe/same/s2.cob (SAME SORT AREA FOR SF1 SF2 PLF with two SORTs USING/GIVING the named plain file) compiles and sorts correctly at 85 and 2002 (s1.cob, LINE SEQUENTIAL, at 2023): CCC BBB AAA after the descending sort. No spec-derived test pins it (unobservable internal procedure) — test-needed. ⚠ For the refuter: the inventory schema's anchor_obliged() makes a CONFORMS DOC row owe its own §7 row unconditionally, while A.1 says this item need not be documented — that tension is filed as a finding (mechanism 'need-not-be-documented A.1 items vs the anchor obligation'). Adjacent SR under-rejection (SAME SORT AREA with no sort file, undeclared operands) is kb/Work PB1087 (open) — a different rule set, not re-reported; GR5 (non-sort files not open during SORT) is a separate rule, not verified here.

A.1 item 172 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 172): required + documented. §13.18.50.3 GR4: 'It is implementor-defined whether the cursor moves as data is entered into a field for which the SECURE clause is specified.' (cite.py --check 13.18.50.3 -> OK 4); A.1 cites it as '13.18.50, SECURE clause, General rule 4'). The SECURE clause is a SCREEN-description clause only (§13.18.50.1: it prevents keyed data 'from appearing on the screen'), part of the ACCEPT/DISPLAY screen handling module A.4.2, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 declares 'Not claimed' (refused by name since 2026-09-02, kb/Work PB260) with §4 item 4. A.1's preamble: 'When the element is part of a feature that is optional or processor-dependent, the item is not required if the optional or processor-dependent feature is not implemented.' So the item cannot arise. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has no DOC-A.1-172 row (correct for a withdrawn item) — but the screen-handling-only derived selector does NOT select this row: its clause arm lists 13.18.50 but the row's own section is A.1 and the selector has no xref-sections arm keyed on the A.1 item's '(13.18.50, ...)' citation (evaluated with scripts/spec/inventory_schema.DerivedSelector: not selected; nor is DOC-A.1-3, another A.4.2 A.1 item). Per the brief, an item unreachable because its module is declined is NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, citing kb/Work A11 (open, the A.1 register). A selector extension (xref-sections 13.18.50 on screen-handling-only, as format-select-when-only does for items 84/85/173) would close it as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT.

A.1 item 181 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 181): OPTIONAL; 'This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented'. §12.3.7.4 GR5: 'The implementor specifies the allowable external-locale-names and the allowable content of literal-4.' (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 -> OK 5)). The element IS PROVIDED: the SPECIAL-NAMES LOCALE clause is implemented (A.4.9 item 10 clause half, owner decision Q1, kb/Work PB64 landed). A determination is WRITTEN, but only in the §4 A.4.9 prose block (docs/CONFORMANCE.md ~line 1088: 'the external identification is a locale TAG — any CLDR locale (BCP-47) or the root spelled INVARIANT — with POSIX spellings normalized (fr_FR.UTF-8 ≡ fr_FR ≡ fr-FR; an @modifier that is a CLDR collation type becomes -u-co-type, any other makes the locale unavailable), and availability is a RUN-TIME property'). §7 has NO DOC-A.1-181 row, so audit_annex_a1.py does not count it and the computed anchor docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-181 resolves to nothing; the prose also never says whether external-locale-name-1 and literal-4 admit the SAME set. Behaviour matches the prose: probe/loc/l1.cob `LOCALE LFR IS "fr_FR.UTF-8"` -> LOCALE-DATE 24/09/2026, `LOCALE LDE IS de-DE` (word form) -> 24.09.2026; l2.cob `LOCALE LXX IS "zz_QQ"` compiles (availability is run-time) and under >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON LOCALE-DATE raises fatal EC-LOCALE-MISSING 'the locale zz-QQ is not available' (unchecked: a default-format result). Determination present but not filed under its own key => DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 181 — NEW finding, same mechanism as DOC-A.1-147 (determination written outside the §7 register).
